# An empty residual gives an averaged normal with a quantified cap cost

This note treats an actual empty residual region. It proves separation
including boundary contact, an explicit endpoint cap-decay estimate, a
genuine fixed-source deformation inequality, and a rank-sensitive circuit
replacement. None of these statements presumes the new cap is critical.

## 1. Exact separation from the open corner

Let d>=2, m=d+1, and let v_0,...,v_d span R^d with sole dependence
sum_i v_i=0. Let T={x:v_i.x<=1 for all i} be the associated simplex.
Let A be a d-dimensional convex body, and fix an index i. Suppose

    R_i=A intersect intersection_(j!=i){x:v_j.x<-1}
        is empty.                                      (1)

Then there exist numbers lambda_j>=0, j!=i, with sum lambda_j=1,
such that the nonzero normal

    u=sum_(j!=i)lambda_j v_j

satisfies

    min_(x in A)u.x>=-1.                               (2)

Here is a complete finite-dimensional separation proof. The d normals
v_j,j!=i, are independent: a dependence extended with zero coefficient
at i would contradict the sole dependence among all m normals. Thus the
affine map x->(v_j.x+1)_(j!=i) is invertible. Let A' be its compact
convex image. It is disjoint from the open negative orthant.

For epsilon>0 let C_epsilon={y:y_j<=-epsilon for all j}. This closed
orthant is disjoint from A'. Choose a closest pair a_epsilon in A'
and c_epsilon in C_epsilon; a pair exists because the distance to that
closed orthant is continuous on compact A', and its nearest point is
the coordinatewise clipping c_j=min(a_j,-epsilon). Set w=a-c. Then
w is nonnegative and nonzero. Minimality against the fixed point c
gives w.(x-a)>=0 for every x in A', by differentiating squared distance
along the segment from a to x. If w_j>0, then c_j=-epsilon. Normalize

    lambda^(epsilon)=w/(sum_j w_j).

It is a probability vector, and every x in A' satisfies

    lambda^(epsilon).x
       >=lambda^(epsilon).a
       =-epsilon+||w||^2/(sum_j w_j)>=-epsilon.

Take a convergent subsequence of these probability vectors as epsilon
decreases to0. Compactness of that finite simplex yields a probability
vector lambda, and taking limits in each displayed inequality gives
lambda.x>=0 for every x in A'. This is exactly(2). Independence of
the d original normals ensures u!=0.

The contact alternatives are precise. If A' is disjoint even from the
closed negative orthant, the same closest-pair argument with epsilon=0
gives min_A u>-1. If A' meets the closed negative orthant, every weak
separator as above has min_A u=-1: at a contact point each coordinate
is nonpositive, while their lambda-weighted sum is nonnegative. Moreover
every positive-weight coordinate vanishes at such a contact point.
Equivalently, if J={j:lambda_j>0}, then every point of
A intersect intersection_(j!=i){v_j.x<=-1} satisfies v_j.x=-1 for j in J.

If every original cut v_j.x=-1 on A is proper, then

    k:=|J|>=2.                                        (3)

Otherwise u would be one original v_j, contradicting the existence
of an A point with v_j.x<-1. Always k<=d.

## 2. The averaged B cap has an explicit k-th order bound

Let B subset T be a d-dimensional convex body, b=|B|, V=|T|. For
epsilon>=0 put

    B_epsilon=B intersect {x:u.x>=1-epsilon}.

Then

    |B_epsilon|<=min{b,C epsilon^k},
    C=V binom(d,k)/[m^k product_(j in J)lambda_j].    (4)

In particular the face at u.x=1 lies in the intersection of the k
corresponding T facets and has affine dimension at most d-k.

To prove(4), use T's ordinary barycentric coordinates
q_j=(1-v_j.x)/m, with q_j>=0 and sum q_j=1. The cap condition is

    sum_(j in J)lambda_j q_j<=epsilon/m.

Uniform volume on T induces constant density d! in any d independent
barycentric coordinates. Integrating the remaining d-k coordinates,
the marginal density on these k coordinates is

    [d!/(d-k)!](1-sum_(j in J)q_j)^(d-k)

on their nonnegative simplex, and zero otherwise. It is at most
d!/(d-k)!. Enlarge the integration domain to the nonnegative weighted
simplex sum lambda_j q_j<=epsilon/m. Its k-volume is
(epsilon/m)^k/[k! product lambda_j]. This proves(4), including k=d.
The epsilon=0 case also follows directly because all positive-weight
slacks must vanish. No smoothness or general-position assumption enters.

## 3. A genuine normal deformation with the new cap's slack retained

Now work with exactly the mixed set

    S=({-1} times A) union ({0} times K) union ({1} times B),

where K is a d-dimensional convex body,0 is interior to K, and
(A+B)/2 subset K. Let Q be the genuine raw halfspace depth at(0,0).
Put

    q_u=|K intersect {u.x>=0}|,
    Delta=a+q_u-Q,                 a=|A|.

By(2), the ambient cap u.x>=z captures all of A at z=-1. By B subset T
and the averaging weights, u.x<=1 throughout B; its level1 boundary
has zero d-volume because u!=0. Therefore this cap has raw mass a+q_u,
and Delta>=0. It is not assumed to attain Q.

For every epsilon>=0, vary the same actual ambient normal to

    u.x>=(1-epsilon)z.

It still contains the source and preserves the middle trace. Its A
capture loses exactly

    L_A(epsilon)=|A intersect {u.x<-1+epsilon}|,

and its B capture is B_epsilon. Genuine source depth therefore gives
the quantitative deformation inequality

    Delta>=L_A(epsilon)-|B_epsilon|
          >=L_A(epsilon)-C epsilon^k.               (5)

All containing halfspaces here are closed. The strict inequality in
the definition of L_A is the exact complement of its closed cap;
the boundary is null since u!=0.

If the averaged cap happens to be critical, Delta=0, its entire
lower A layer must obey

    L_A(epsilon)<=C epsilon^k for all epsilon>=0.     (6)

Thus the empty residual has provided a genuine endpoint deformation
and an explicit order constraint, not merely a separating hyperplane.

## 4. Contact dimension forces a positive inactive-cap slack

Assume min_A u=-1 and let F=A intersect {u.x=-1} be the exposed
minimum face. Suppose its affine dimension is r>d-k. Then Delta is
strictly positive, with an explicit lower bound described below.
In particular, if the averaged cap is critical, necessarily

    dim_aff(F)<=d-k.                                 (7)

Choose r+1 affinely independent actual points of F. Extend them to
d+1 affinely independent points of A by choosing the remaining
p=d-r points in int(A); this is possible successively because int(A)
is an open full-dimensional set. Let D be their full d-simplex, of
volume V_D>0. The p added vertices have strictly positive heights
u.x+1. Put H_* equal to their maximum height. The other r+1 vertices
have height0.

In barycentric coordinates of D, the height is at most H_* times
the sum of the p added-vertex coordinates. For0<epsilon<=H_*/2,
the part of D where those coordinates sum to at most epsilon/H_*
therefore lies in A's lower layer, up to its null boundary. Their
marginal density relative to uniform volume on D is

    [d!/r!](1-sum q)^{r}>=d!/(r! 2^r)

on this small simplex. Consequently

    L_A(epsilon)>=L epsilon^p,
    L=V_D binom(d,p)/(2^r H_*^p)>0.                 (8)

Since r>d-k means p<k, define

    epsilon_* =min{H_*/2,(L/(2C))^(1/(k-p))}>0.

Combining(5) and(8) proves

    Delta>=(L/2)epsilon_*^p>0.                       (9)

This also verifies(7) without using an unproved cap asymptotic.

There is a convenient facet version. If r=d-1 and
sigma=H_(d-1)(F)/||u||>0, put H_A=max_A u+1. The actual cone from
the whole face F to a point attaining height H_A lies in A, so
for0<=epsilon<=H_A/2,

    L_A(epsilon)>=sigma epsilon/2^(d-1).

With L_f=sigma/2^(d-1) and
epsilon_f=min{H_A/2,(L_f/(2C))^(1/(k-1))}, equation(5) gives the
explicit positive slack Delta>=L_f epsilon_f/2. This uses the actual
facet measure, not an assumed differentiability of A.

## 5. Exact circuit replacement and its accounted mass cost

Extend the weight vector by lambda_i=0. Let

    L_0=max_j lambda_j,
    M={j:lambda_j=L_0},             p_0=|M|.

Replace the p_0 normals indexed by M by u, keeping all v_j with
j outside M. Their positive dependence is exactly

    (1/L_0)u+sum_(j notin M)(1-lambda_j/L_0)v_j=0.   (10)

All displayed coefficients are positive. The remaining m-p_0 original
normals are independent, and(10) expresses u in their span. Therefore
the new family is a minimal positive circuit of rank

    m-p_0=d+1-p_0.

Its continuous halfspaces through0 cover the entire ambient space.
If p_0>=2 this is an actual rank reduction; if p_0=1 there is no
rank reduction. Neither multiplicity case is presumed in advance.

The coefficient sum in(10) is exactly m, because sum lambda_j=1.
Thus replacing continuous normals in the ambient normals(-1,v_j)
preserves their total integer component -m as well as the zero
continuous sum.

If all original caps v_j.x>=z are critical with common mass Q, the
new averaged cap has mass Q+Delta. Therefore the weighted cap mass
of the replaced family is exactly

    mQ+Delta/L_0.                                    (11)

This cost cannot be discarded. In particular(10) alone does not create
a smaller critical cap cover: the cap which captures all of A may be
strictly inactive, and Sections3--4 quantify when it must be inactive.

## Scope

The note supplies an actual supporting normal, explicit boundary-contact
alternatives, a B-cap power bound, a proved deformation gain when the A
contact face is too large, and a rank-sensitive replacement with its
exact slack cost. It does not assert that every empty-residual separator
has boundary contact, that its cap is critical, or that its maximal
weights tie. Eliminating these remaining alternatives would require a
further argument; no OC conclusion is inferred here.

There is nevertheless a useful proved choice under a bad-source premise.
Section5 of
`candidate 5dd69a77cceb0773`
shows that nonemptiness of ALL CLOSED corner regions already forces
the strict depth margin Q/M>3Gamma_d/5 in the exact proper-A/zero-B
critical circuit. Thus a source with Q<=Gamma_d M/2 has at least one
empty closed corner. Selecting that index in Section1 gives a strict
separation min_A u>-1. This does not make its averaged cap critical
or erase its Delta cost; it identifies which boundary alternative is
available for a hypothetical bad source.
